Oct. 30: Packers' ground game cause for concern

By Adam Rank

Jordan Love throws multiple touchdown passes. Matthew Golden looks good. I mean, Christian Watson left and arrived back at Lambeau Field from an ambulance in a move that would make Triple H say, "no way this is real." And yet, I get a note from my editor (a Packers fan, mind you) complaining about the (lack of a) Green Bay Packers running game.

I mean, the Milwaukee Brewers just won the World Series, but we need to focus on the Packers' rushing attack? Well, I guess that is the best place to start.

The Packers won the game despite rushing for just 66 yards. They have been held to fewer than 90 rushing yards in all eight games, the club's longest streak in the Super Bowl era. The Packers' 485 rushing yards are the fewest by any team through eight games since the 2019 Bengals. I mean, what in the name of Eddie Lee Ivery is going on here?

The short answer is the offensive line is bad. The playcalling is bad. I mean, you think the guy who favored Dion Lewis over Derrick Henry when he was offensive coordinator in Tennessee was ever going to have a solid running game in Green Bay? It's just the facts.

And it's not going to get much easier in the coming weeks, either. The New England Patriots, Minnesota Vikings and Los Angeles Rams aren't great matchups. It's not until the New Orleans Saints in Week 13 that the schedule softens for Josh Jacobs. If you kept him on your roster all this time, you're likely going to be compelled to start him, but the matchups aren't ideal.

Some other notes from Thursday night:

Love has accounted for multiple touchdowns in all eight games this season, but this was his first game of the season with three touchdown passes. He's a set-and-forget quarterback moving forward. It is wild to think he wasn't drafted as a QB1 this year.
Watson is nearing ace territory this season. He recorded his 12th reception of 20-plus yards, second in the league behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba.
Golden is also a must-start, but he registered two drops Thursday. Love has seen 20 drops by his receivers this season. I feel like that total would double if you counted the number of interceptions that are dropped. Or maybe it just seems that way to me, a Bears supporter.
Is the "Bryce Young as a QB1" era over already? Well, for starters, the Carolina Panthers need to do a better job of protecting him. He was hit. A lot. I'm not rushing him back into my lineup next week against the Denver Broncos. You might want to take a look at the waiver wire right now for a streamable option if Young is your only quarterback. Kyler Murray against the Buffalo Bills next week could do the trick.
Chuba Hubbard was good, however. He scored a touchdown, rushed for 81 yards and caught seven balls for 38 more yards. Again, playing the Bills next week makes him a prime RB1.

stories.headline: Astros owner Jim Crane hails Randy Flores as a 'perfect fit' as team's GM
stories.summary: Randy Flores was introduced as the 15th general manager of the Astros on Monday.
stories.body:
HOUSTON -- The Astros interviewed a variety of candidates in the search for their next general manager.

It quickly became clear that Randy Flores was their guy.

"We went over it and over it and over it and as we reflected back on everybody we spoke to and the qualities, we were looking for Randy was a perfect fit," Astros owner Jim Crane said Monday. "He has experience in every single area of baseball, and you don't find that very often and he has been trained and been around some good organizations. So, he stood out at the end."

Flores was introduced as the 15th general manager of the Astros on Monday after being hired on Friday to replace Dana Brown, who was let go in August with his contract set to expire at the end of the season.

The Astros cut ties with Brown on Aug. 24. Three assistant general managers and Hall of Famer and special adviser Jeff Bagwell took over his responsibilities for the remainder of the season while Crane sought a replacement.

Flores had been serving as the St. Louis Cardinals' assistant general manager of amateur and pro acquisition.

The former major league pitcher joined the Cardinals' front office as director of scouting in 2015 and spent eight seasons (2019-26) as an assistant GM with the club.

He said there is a mixture of excitement and nerves as well as another emotion as he embarks on his first general manager job.

"There's a weight to the role," he said. "Does that make sense? A weight and a responsibility. That's what I feel right now, actually."

His first order of business will be hiring a manager after Joe Espada's contract was not renewed after the AL West Champions were swept by the Chicago White Sox in their Wild Card Series.

Flores said he'll get to work on that task immediately and shared some things he'll be looking for when filling that position.

"The qualities you look for, in coordination with Jim, we're talking about trust, we're talking about energy, we're talking about chemistry," he said.

Crane added that he interviewed a few managerial candidates before hiring Flores.

"But now that we've got Randy in place, he'll take over that process along with our team and we'll get to work on that," he said. "We hope to get that filled very quickly."

After that they'll set their sights on working on the roster for next season. And Crane said he doesn't envision it being a rebuilding year.

"I don't think it's going to be a complete tear down at all," he said. "I think we've got enough talent to work with, and we've got to make some good decisions and make some changes and solidify a better lineup and a better team than we had last year."

He pointed out that even though the season had a disappointing ending, Houston did return to the postseason after missing out the previous year. The Astros went 81-81 to win the AL West for the fifth time in six years, becoming the first big league club without a winning record to reach the playoffs in a non-shortened season.

"We did make the playoffs, which is always the goal," Crane said. "But we have very high standards here and so I'm sure these guys will get together and make some good decisions, and you'll see some changes made with the roster, surely."

Flores pitched in the majors for eight seasons from 2002-10, going 11-5 with a 4.61 ERA and four saves. The left-hander made 347 relief appearances and three starts for Texas, Colorado, St. Louis and Minnesota.

Crane likes that Flores played professionally, a quality that very few MLB general managers have. Additionally, Crane, who made his fortune as a shipping magnate, was impressed with all of the different roles Flores has served in the Cardinals front office.

"His resume is so complete that you very rarely find a guy that's worked in every single department," Crane said. "I started on the dock in my business and made it to the top. So, I think it's very important to know how everything functions and what those people are doing and how they're doing it and determine if they're doing it well or not doing it well."

Flores said the quality from his playing days that he thinks will help him succeed in his new role is his competitiveness.

"I'm competitive," he said. "We're all competitive in this game. Otherwise, why do this job ... we want development, we want process, but ultimately every night there's a real game. It's not expected outcomes. It's not probabilities. It's a win and a loss, and there's 162 of them, and I can't wait to be in that fight with this team."

stories.headline: Where do 2026 champion Valkyries rank among every WNBA title team?
stories.summary: Las Vegas' 2023 title team topped our rankings two years ago. Where do the 2026 Valkyries fit in?
stories.body:
On Saturday, the Golden State Valkyries won the 2026 WNBA title in just their second year to put the finishing touches on the league's 30th season. Where do they rank among all of the WNBA champions?

The Valkyries built their reputation on being a complete team that relied on defense. At 67.4 points per game, they had the lowest scoring average in the Finals of any champion since Sacramento (66.8 PPG) in 2005. Golden State is also one of just five WNBA champions that averaged fewer points in the WNBA Finals than the team it defeated for the title.

But the Valkyries lit up the Bay Area Halloween celebrations with their thrilling second-half comeback victory in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals. The league went to a best-of-seven format for the Finals in 2025, but this year was the first to go the distance. The No. 2 seed Valkyries won three times at home at Chase Center in the series and once on the road at State Farm Arena.

Gabby Williams, in her first year with Golden State, was the Valkyries' go-to player who performed offensively at a superstar level in the postseason. She averaged 21.0 points in 13 playoff games, including five of 25 points or more. Her 30 points in Game 7 helped secure the WNBA Finals MVP award. In those seven games, she averaged 19.6 points, which ranks 19th among the 30 Finals MVPs.

The Valkyries did it their way: 100% committed to defense and a process that worked all season. And even though they don't rank in the top 10 all time, being anywhere on this list is great because these teams are all the ultimate winners.

1. 2023 Las Vegas Aces
Regular-season and playoff records: 34-6, 8-1

Defeated the New York Liberty 3-1 in Finals

As good as they were in winning the 2022 championship, the Aces were even better in 2023. They ranked No. 1 in scoring and defense during the Regular-season and stumbled just once in the playoffs, in Game 3 of the Finals. A'ja Wilson got her first WNBA Finals MVP honor for her performance in 2023; she won again for the 2025 Finals.

In Chelsea Gray, Kelsey Plum and Jackie Young, the Aces also had trio of guards who were among the best backcourts in league history.

Candace Parker, a free agent signee who was expected to be a big part of the Aces' 2023 title run, was sidelined by foot surgery that July. The Aces also lost starters Gray and Kiah Stokes before Game 4 and still won the title, illustrating how good the chemistry was for the team. The Las Vegas bench -- then led by Alysha Clark, Cayla George, Sydney Colson and Kierstan Bell -- came through when they were needed most.

2. 2000 Houston Comets

Regular-season and playoff records: 27-5, 6-0

Defeated the New York Liberty 2-0 in Finals

This was the last of Houston's four consecutive title teams, the end of the Comets' version of "Camelot." In 2000, the WNBA was at 16 teams and most of the former ABL players were in their second year in the league. Sheryl Swoopes won her first of three MVP awards and two-time MVP Cynthia Cooper played her last full season at age 37.

As was the case with the other Houston championship teams, the stars carried them: Swoopes and Cooper averaged 35 minutes a game, Tina Thompson 34 and Janeth Arcain 30.5. Fifth starter, Tiffani Johnson (22.2), was the only other player who averaged at least 20 minutes a game. With three future Hall of Famers (Cooper, Swoopes, Thompson), Houston didn't need much statistically from its reserves. The Comets' bench players knew their roles, and the team knew how to win. This title ended the dynasty -- the Los Angeles Sparks were ascending -- but what a finish.

3. 2020 Seattle Storm

Regular-season and playoff records: 18-4, 6-0

Defeated the Las Vegas Aces 3-0 in Finals

Point guard Sue Bird, part of all four Storm title teams, has ruminated over which of them was "best." Lauren Jackson was the superstar of the 2004 and 2010 Storm title teams; her counterpart in 2018 and 2020 was Breanna Stewart. Bird said an edge goes to the very similarly constructed 2018 and 2020 teams due to the presence of guard Jewell Loyd. Bird then gives a nod to the overall depth and chemistry to the 2020 Storm, who were first in the league in offensive and defensive rating.

"The way we shot 3's, the way we moved the ball -- if you took something away, we'd just keep it moving," Bird said. "We talked before every game that we were going to wear teams out with the pace that we played."

4. 2013 Minnesota Lynx

Regular-season and playoff records: 26-8, 7-0

Defeated the Atlanta Dream 3-0 in Finals

This was the second of four Lynx titles in a seven-season span. They didn't have the best regular-season record among Lynx champs; both 2011 and 2017 went 27-7 (and the 2016 runners-up were 28-6). But coach Cheryl Reeve said the "core four" of the franchise -- Seimone Augustus, Rebekkah Brunson, Maya Moore and Lindsay Whalen -- were near the peak of their collective powers in 2013. They all averaged double figures in scoring, led by Moore's 18.5 PPG. The fifth starter was Janel McCarville, Whalen's former University of Minnesota teammate, and that pairing again thrilled Gophers fans.

In 2012, Minnesota lost 3-1 in the Finals to Indiana, which irked the Lynx because they were five games better than the Fever in the regular-season standings. The 2013 team didn't allow any openings in the playoffs, sweeping Seattle, Phoenix and Atlanta.

5. 1998 Houston Comets

Regular-season and playoff records: 27-3, 4-1

Defeated the Phoenix Mercury 2-1 in Finals

Cooper said if she had to pick just one Comets championship team as her favorite, it would be this one. The team's .900 winning percentage (27-3) remains the best in WNBA history. Swoopes was second on the team in scoring at 15.6 PPG to Cooper's 22.7. Cooper won her second consecutive MVP award; she was Finals MVP for all four championship teams.

And there's another reason this team is dear to Cooper's heart. Her close friend, Kim Perrot, the Comets' spark plug point guard, averaged 8.5 points and 4.7 assists in what would be her last season in the WNBA. Perrot had 13 points, five rebounds and four assists in the title-clinching win over the Mercury. Five months later, she was diagnosed with cancer and died in August 1999 at age 32.

6. 2014 Phoenix Mercury

Regular-season and playoff records: 29-5, 7-1

Defeated the Chicago Sky 3-0 in Finals

Amid the Lynx dynasty from 2011 to 2017, the Mercury owned this season. Their 29 wins was a WNBA record at that time, and they were first in offensive and defensive rating. All five starters -- Diana Taurasi, Brittney Griner, Candice Dupree, Penny Taylor and DeWanna Bonner -- averaged double digits in scoring.

Their only loss in the playoffs came to Minnesota in Game 2 of the Western Conference finals, but they bounced back to win the series with an 18-point Game 3 victory. In the WNBA Finals, Chicago was no match. Taurasi, who averaged 16.2 PPG in the Regular-season and 21.9 PPG in the playoffs, was WNBA Finals MVP for the second time.

7. 2017 Minnesota Lynx

Regular-season and playoff records: 27-7, 6-2

Defeated the Los Angeles Sparks 3-2 in Finals

Minnesota was still smarting over a 3-2 Finals loss to Los Angeles in 2016, and the teams were again archrivals in 2017. Minnesota was first in the league in offensive and defensive rating and Los Angeles was second in both.

Target Center was being renovated, so the Lynx's home games in the 2017 playoffs were at the University of Minnesota' Williams Arena, where Whalen had played in college. The decisive 85-76 Game 5 win came in a packed and cacophonous Williams, and Fowles was Finals MVP for a second time (she also won in 2015).

8. 2019 Washington Mystics

Regular-season and playoff records: 26-8, 6-3

Defeated the Connecticut Sun 3-2 in Finals

Elena Delle Donne said this was the best team she has ever played on: "Not just talent-wise, but the way emotionally and mentally we were so on-point with one another. That's what took us to the next level."

The Mystics were more dominant in the Regular-season than the playoffs, but had to overcome a back injury that hampered Delle Donne during the Finals. She was the MVP in 2019, but teammate Emma Meesseman was the Finals MVP, averaging 17.8 points in the championship series.

9. 2022 Las Vegas Aces
Regular-season and playoff records: 26-10, 8-2

Defeated the Connecticut Sun 3-1 in Finals

The 2022 Aces ran into more challenges in the Regular-season than the 2023 version of Las Vegas. But by the playoffs, they were in control as the league's best team.

In coach Becky Hammon's first season with the franchise, the Aces changed their playing style -- 3-pointers became a far bigger part of the offense -- and Plum and Young matured into even better players. Wilson won her second regular-season MVP award and was Defensive Player of the Year. Then Gray was on fire throughout the playoffs, winning Finals MVP.

It was a big achievement for a franchise that started when the league did in 1997, in Utah, moved to San Antonio, and then found its championship home in Las Vegas under owner Mark Davis. He paid top dollar to bring Hammon from the NBA, where she was a San Antonio Spurs assistant, and it was a great investment.

10. 1999 Houston Comets

Regular-season and playoff records: 26-6, 4-2

Defeated the New York Liberty 2-1 in Finals

In 1999, almost all the former ABL standouts had transitioned into and strengthened the WNBA. That didn't stop the Comets, who added former ABL player Sonja Henning at point guard. Houston's standouts were the same as in 1998: Cooper, Swoopes and Thompson. Bulgarian center Polina Tzekova, then 31, made the most of her only WNBA season, starting every game for Houston in 1999.

Ultimately, there was a melancholy feel to the 1999 championship for the Comets. Their former point guard Perrot died from cancer on Aug. 19. After being stunned by Liberty guard Teresa Weatherspoon's buzzer-beating halfcourt heave in Game 2 of the Finals, Houston won Game 3 and secured its third title in honor of Perrot.

11. 2024 New York Liberty
Regular-season and playoff records: 32-8, 8-3

Defeated the Minnesota Lynx 3-2 in Finals

It took 27 years since the launch of the Liberty as an original WNBA franchise in 1997, but New York finally broke through for its first championship. After finishing with the best record in the league, the Liberty defeated defending champion Las Vegas in the semifinals and then avenged a Commissioner's Cup final loss to Minnesota in the Finals.

The deciding Game 5 vs. the Lynx nearly extended the Liberty's long postseason heartbreak. But a late foul (still disputed by Minnesota) sent Breanna Stewart to the line. She scored the tying points to send the game into overtime, where New York prevailed 67-62.

Jonquel Jones won the Finals MVP honor as she got her first title. Sabrina Ionescu also won the championship for the first time. It was the third title for Stewart, who won two championships in Seattle.

12. 2001 Los Angeles Sparks

Regular-season and playoff records: 28-4, 6-1

Defeated the Charlotte Sting 2-0 in Finals

The Sparks learned a lot going against Houston for four seasons before making their championship breakthrough. Los Angeles star Lisa Leslie has joked, "Thank God that Coop retired," in reference to the Houston's Cooper ending her playing career after the 2000 season (she returned for four games in 2003 at age 40).

Leslie, Mwadi Mabika, Tamecka Dixon and DeLisha Milton-Jones all averaged in double figures during this title run. Leslie was MVP for the season and the Finals.

13. 2011 Minnesota Lynx

Regular-season and playoff records: 27-7, 7-1

Defeated the Atlanta Dream 3-0 in Finals

In 2010, Minnesota got a new coach (Reeve) and also added Whalen (trade) and Brunson (Sacramento dispersal draft). The next year brought the opening championship of the Lynx dynasty as No. 1 pick Moore was Rookie of the Year. The 22-year-old Moore started alongside Taj McWilliams-Franklin, who turned 41 two weeks after the Finals ended. This Lynx team really spanned the age/experience gamut.

The season also brought a well-deserved spotlight to Augustus, who became the original building block for the dynasty when she was drafted No. 1 in 2006. She led the 2011 Lynx in scoring in the Regular-season (16.2) and playoffs (22.0) and was the Finals MVP.

14. 2016 Los Angeles Sparks

Regular-season and playoff records: 26-8, 6-3

Defeated the Minnesota Lynx 3-2 in Finals

After winning back-to-back titles in 2001-02, the Sparks endured a lot of frustrating "almost" in the playoffs. They lost in the WNBA Finals in 2003 and the conference finals in 2006, 2008, 2009 and 2012. The playoff format changed in 2016, seeding the top eight teams regardless of conference, and the Sparks made the Finals again. In an epic five-game series, they beat Minnesota 77-76 on Nneka Ogwumike's putback with 3.1 seconds remaining. Ogwumike was the season MVP and teammate Candace Parker the Finals MVP. It was the last jewel to complete Parker's crown; she already had won two NCAA titles and two Olympic gold medals.

15. 2025 Las Vegas Aces
Regular-season and playoff records: 30-14, 9-3

Defeated the Phoenix Mercury 4-0 in Finals

The 2025 Aces might be the most difficult champion to rank because the first half of their five-month season (counting playoffs) was so different from the second half. But some key factors elevate them to the middle of the pack in the rankings.

The first is the play of Wilson, who won her fourth regular-season MVP and second Finals MVP. During the playoffs, she averaged 26.8 PPG, 10.0 RPG, 3.3 assists and 2.5 blocks. Her postseason performance was even greater than in the Regular-season. She also hit the most crucial shot of the Finals: the game winner with less than a second left in Game 3 to give the Aces a 90-88 victory.

The Aces also got a terrific postseason from guards Jackie Young (20.4 PPG, 5.5 APG) and Chelsea Gray (11.2 PPG, 7.3 APG).

The Aces' 17-game winning streak (counting Game 1 of the playoffs) is the second longest in WNBA history. And coach Becky Hammon led the Aces to a third championship in four years despite having to replace a key player (guard Kelsey Plum) from the first two title teams. The Aces are the league's ultimate example that it's not how you start, it's how you finish.

16. 2018 Seattle Storm

Regular-season and playoff records: 26-8, 6-2

Defeated the Washington Mystics 3-0 in Finals

History repeated itself with the Storm. They had back-to-back No. 1 picks in Jackson and Bird in 2001 and 2002, which led to two titles. Seattle again got consecutive No. 1s in 2015 and 2016 with Loyd and Stewart, which also led to two titles. This 2018 championship in a lot of ways was won in the semifinals, when the Storm held off Phoenix in an epic Game 5 in which Bird took over in the fourth quarter. In the finals, Seattle wasn't going to be denied and swept the Mystics. And the Storm looked to be a strong threat to become the first repeat champion since the Sparks in 2001-02. But an Achilles injury kept Stewart out in 2019. When she returned in 2020, the Storm picked up where they had left off in 2018.

17. 2010 Seattle Storm

Regular-season and playoff records: 28-6, 7-0

Defeated the Atlanta Dream 3-0 in Finals

The 2010 Storm were six games better than any team in the WNBA; no other team in the Western Conference even had a winning record. Jackson won her third MVP award, and she and Bird got to celebrate their second WNBA championship together. Bird, Swin Cash and Svetlana Abrosimova, who had won an NCAA title together at UConn in 2000, all played for this Storm team. Seattle didn't lose at home in 2010, which ended up being Jackson's last full season in the WNBA, as injuries forced her out of the league after 2012.

18. 2005 Sacramento Monarchs

Regular-season and playoff records: 25-9, 7-1

Defeated the Connecticut Sun 3-1 in Finals

After losing in the conference finals three of the previous four years, the Monarchs won in 2005.

At age 29, Yolanda Griffith entered the WNBA in 1999 from the ABL and was her new league's MVP that year, a perfect target for point guard Ticha Penicheiro.

Griffith also won Finals MVP, and it was a career-best year for DeMya Walker, who led the Monarchs in scoring in the Regular-season and made an All-Star appearance. This was also the first of Rebekkah Brunson's five WNBA titles; her other four came with Minnesota.

19. 2002 Los Angeles Sparks

Regular-season and playoff records: 25-7, 6-0

Defeated the New York Liberty 2-0 in Finals

The Sparks' repeat championship seemed more predictable than extraordinary at the time, coming after Houston had won four in a row. But it took two decades for another franchise to go back-to-back, with the Aces doing it in 2022-2023. That makes Los Angeles' achievement stand out more now. There isn't much to separate this Sparks team from the 2001 Sparks, who had a little better regular-season record (28-4 in 2001 to 25-7 in 2002). The standout players were the same except for Nikki Teasley, a rookie in 2002 who hit the championship-clinching 3-pointer in Game 2 of the Finals.

20. 2026 Golden State Valkyries

Regular-season and playoff records: 32-12, 9-4

Defeated the Atlanta Dream 4-3 in Finals

Much has been made of the Valkyries being the first champions without any All-WNBA selections in the season they won the title. They also are the first team since the 2013 Minnesota Lynx to not have a current or former season MVP on the roster at the time of their championship.

This largely reflects the Valkyries' focus on defense: The All-WNBA first and second teams are generally tilted toward big offensive stats. So a lot of credit must go to Golden State's team chemistry and an outstanding coaching job by Natalie Nakase and her staff.

In the playoffs, the Valkyries beat teams with some of the top offensive players in the league: Dallas' Paige Bueckers and Arike Ogunbowale, Las Vegas' A'ja Wilson, Jackie Young and Chelsea Gray, and Atlanta's Rhyne Howard and Allisha Gray.

As mentioned, the Valkyries are one of five WNBA champions who averaged fewer points in the Finals than their opponent (67.4 PPG to Atlanta's 71.4); the others are Las Vegas (2022), Los Angeles (2016), and Detroit twice (2006, 2003). But the Dream's Finals scoring average was still 20 points lower than their regular-season average, plus Golden State held Atlanta under 65 points in all four of its victories.

It was very impressive, and as time passes, the Valkyries' performance might move up even more in historical regard.

21. 2006 Detroit Shock

Regular-season and playoff records: 23-11, 7-3

Defeated the Sacramento Monarchs 3-2 in Finals

A big key for this team was the 2005 midseason trade that brought Katie Smith to the Shock. She fit in well with Cash, Cheryl Ford, Deanna Nolan and Ruth Riley, who were all on Detroit's 2003 championship squad.

Nolan, a native of nearby Flint, Michigan, was Finals MVP as the Shock prevented Sacramento's attempt at a repeat. In the decisive Game 5, won 80-75 by Detroit, Nolan played all 40 minutes and scored 24 points.

22. 2012 Indiana Fever

Regular-season and playoff records: 22-12, 7-3

Defeated the Minnesota Lynx 3-1 in Finals

When Indiana lost its playoff opener 75-66 at home to Atlanta, there was no reason to think anything magical was in the works. Yet the Fever won the next two games and the series. The Fever also lost their opener in the East finals to Connecticut, but won 2-1 again.

Next up: A Lynx team that had the best record in the league that year. The Fever and Lynx split the first two games of the Finals. But in Game 3, the Lynx -- who led the league in offensive rating -- were held to a season-low 59 points.

Indiana had been up 2-1 in the 2009 Finals yet lost the series to Phoenix. But in 2012, franchise legend Tamika Catchings got her long-awaited title as the Fever won Game 4 at home.

23. 2007 Phoenix Mercury

Regular-season and playoff records: 23-11, 7-2

Defeated the Detroit Shock 3-2 in Finals

Three years after winning her third title at UConn, Taurasi won her first WNBA championship. Phoenix's winning formula was coach Paul Westhead's run-and-gun offense, which was first in the league. Defense was not as much a priority; the Mercury were next-to-last in defensive rating. But it worked, with Taurasi, Taylor, Cappie Pondexter and Tangela Smith all averaging double digits in scoring.

The Finals matchup with defending champion Detroit got chippy, with Phoenix surviving a physical Game 4 in a 77-76 win. Then the Mercury became the first WNBA team to win a championship on the road, taking Game 5 108-92 at Detroit behind 30 points from Taylor -- who went 18 of 18 from the free throw line -- and 26 points and 10 assists from Finals MVP Pondexter.

24. 2004 Seattle Storm

Regular-season and playoff records: 20-14, 6-2

Defeated the Connecticut Sun 2-1 in Finals

This was Seattle's first trip to the WNBA Finals. And this was the last year that the Finals was a best-of-three series. The Storm were on the ropes after a 68-64 opening loss at Connecticut. But they pulled out a 67-65 nail-biter in Game 2 at Seattle, led by Betty Lennox's 27 points. In Game 3, with KeyArena packed with Storm fans wielding thunder sticks, Lennox had 23 points and earned Finals MVP honors as Seattle clinched the title 74-60.

25. 2015 Minnesota Lynx

Regular-season and playoff records: 22-12, 7-3

Defeated the Indiana Fever 3-2 in Finals

Of the Lynx's four title teams, this was the only one with double-digit losses, as Augustus and Whalen both dealt with injuries. But big-time help came via two trades in July: first for guard Renee Montgomery and then for center Sylvia Fowles, who had sat out the season to that point to force a trade from Chicago.

Moore, the 2014 MVP, was again brilliant in 2015, leading the Lynx in scoring in the Regular-season (20.6 PPG) and the postseason (23.4). She hit a buzzer-beating 3-pointer to win Game 3 of the Finals vs. Indiana 80-77. The Fever won Game 4, but Fowles cemented her Finals MVP award with 20 points and 11 rebounds in a Game 5 victory.

26. 2009 Phoenix Mercury

Regular-season and playoff records: 23-11, 7-4

Defeated the Indiana Fever 3-2 in Finals

This was a good team led by a great player in Taurasi, who won her only regular-season MVP award in 2009. Like the 2007 champions, the Mercury focused on outscoring foes: Phoenix was first in offensive rating and last in defensive rating. Five players averaged in double figures, led by Taurasi's 20.4 PPG and Pondexter's 19.1.

The first game of the 2009 Finals was amazing: a 120-116 Mercury victory over Indiana. But the Fever took the next two games and had a chance to close out the series at home. Phoenix's defense showed up for Game 4, holding the Fever to a series-low 77 points. In Game 5, Taurasi and Pondexter combined for 50 points to win their last game as Phoenix teammates. Pondexter requested and got a trade to New York the next year.

27. 2021 Chicago Sky
Regular-season and playoff records: 16-16, 8-2

Defeated the Phoenix Mercury 3-1 in Finals

With longtime Sparks star Candace Parker coming to her hometown of Chicago as a free agent, there were big expectations for the 2021 Sky. Chicago went .500 in the Regular-season, the worst record of any championship team. But all the pieces were there -- including point guard Courtney Vandersloot and guard/forward Kahleah Copper -- to win a title.

The No. 6 seed, the Sky beat Dallas in the first round and Minnesota in the second. Then they went against No. 1 seed Connecticut in the semifinals. A double-overtime win in the first game of the series was pivotal, and Chicago won 3-1. In the Finals, the Sky won 3-1 over Phoenix, with Parker celebrating with family as the franchise won its first title.

28. 1997 Houston Comets

Regular-season and playoff records: 18-10, 2-0

Defeated the New York Liberty in championship game

This is where it all started, with the Comets winning the inaugural championship of the WNBA, which launched with eight teams. Cooper at age 34 was the best player in the new league, averaging 22.2 points and being named MVP. They played just single-game semifinals and finals in the first year, and Cooper scored 31 and 25 points in those victories. Thompson, who had been the top pick in the college draft, averaged 13.2 points and Brazil's Arcain 10.9. Swoopes gave birth to a son on June 25, just after the WNBA season had started. She played her first game on Aug. 7, and appeared in nine regular-season and two playoff games.

29. 2008 Detroit Shock

Regular-season and playoff records: 22-12, 7-2

Defeated the San Antonio Silver Stars 3-0 in Finals

By the time the Stars met the Shock in the WNBA Finals, Detroit was the better team. Five Shock players averaged in double figures in the Regular-season, led by Nolan and Smith. A late-season trade brought McWilliams-Franklin to Detroit, and she averaged 12.9 points and 7.8 rebounds in the playoffs. Smith won Finals MVP honors as the Shock won their third WNBA title in six years.

Unfortunately, the franchise was nearing its end in Detroit. The Shock played just one more season in the Motor City before moving to Tulsa in 2010.

30. 2003 Detroit Shock

Regular-season and playoff records: 25-9, 6-2

Defeated the Los Angeles Sparks 2-1 in Finals

The Shock went from worst in 2002 (9-23) to first in 2003, ending the Sparks' attempt to three-peat. Former Pistons player Bill Laimbeer took over as Shock coach during the 2002 season and totally changed the team's culture. He drafted Cheryl Ford at No. 3 in 2003; she averaged a double-double (10.8 PPG, 10.4 RPG) and was Rookie of the Year. Cash, who had been the No. 2 pick in 2002, led the Shock with 16.6 points in the Regular-season and 16.3 in the playoffs.

Detroit lost the Finals opener to Los Angeles, but survived Game 2, winning 62-61. In front of a huge crowd at The Palace at Auburn Hills, the Shock took the title in Game 3 in an 83-78 win, led by 27 points from Finals MVP Ruth Riley and Cash's near triple-double (13 points, 12 rebounds, 9 assists).

"I think our team really embodied the city of Detroit," Cash said.

stories.headline: São Paulo Grand Prix 2026: Race in Brazil start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions
stories.summary: Formula 1 heads to Brazil for the São Paulo Grand Prix, a week after Kimi Antonelli was crowned world champion.
stories.body:
Formula 1 heads to Brazil for the São Paulo Grand Prix, a week after Kimi Antonelli was crowned world champion.

The Mercedes driver finished the Mexico City Grand Prix in third and made history by becoming Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the race, with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton behind in second.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 20th round.

- The families that built Kimi Antonelli, F1 world champion

- How Kimi Antonelli overcame George Russell, Ferrari to become F1's youngest champion

- Kimi Antonelli's historic F1 title: Every record broken and milestone reached

São Paulo Grand Prix schedule
All times in GMT

Friday, November 6

Practice One: 3.30 p.m. - 4.30 p.m.

Practice Two: 7 p.m. - 8 p.m.

Saturday, November 7

Final Practice: 2.30 p.m. - 3.30 p.m.

Qualifying: 6 p.m. - 7 p.m.

Sunday, November 8

São Paulo Grand Prix: 5 p.m.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the São Paulo Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Autódromo José Carlos Pace
Situated in a neighbourhood between two artificial lakes, Interlagos (which translates to "between lakes"), first opened as a race track in 1940. Formula 1 first raced at the circuit in 1972 as a non-championship race before becoming part of the calendar from 1973.

It dropped off the calendar in 1980 after its bumpy surface was considered dangerous, but F1 returned to a shortened and updated version of the circuit in 1990, which coincided with the rise of Ayrton Senna to global stardom. Senna's S at Turn 1 is one of the best overtaking spots on the track.

The circuit is one of the drivers and fans favourites. It's short, undulating nature, mixed with changing weather, often produces a blockbuster race.

São Paulo Grand Prix

Circuit: Autódromo José Carlos Pace; São Paulo, Brazil

Previous winners in São Paulo

2014: Nico Rosberg (Mercedes)

2015: Nico Rosberg (Mercedes)

2016: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2017: Sebastian Vettel (Ferrari)

2018: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2019: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2021: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2022: George Russell (Mercedes)

2023: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2024: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2025: Lando Norris (McLaren)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 1973

Laps: 71 laps of 4.3km

Lap record: 1:10.540, Valtteri Bottas (2018)

Most wins: Alain Prost with six at Interlagos & Jacarepagua (1982-1984-1985, 1987-1988, 1990) and Michael Schumacher has four at this circuit (1994-1995, 2000-2002). Other winners from the current grid are Hamilton (2016, 2018, 2021), Verstappen (2019, 2023, 2024), George Russell (2022) and Lando Norris (2025).

Most poles: Ayrton Senna with six (1986, 1988-1991, 1994). Previous pole sitters on the current grid are Fernando Alonso (2005), Hamilton (2012, 2016, 2018), Russell (2022), Verstappen (2019, 2023) and Norris (2024 and 2025).

Weather forecast

The weather for the São Paulo Grand Prix is due to be cloudy during Friday's practice, with thundery showers forecast on Saturday with highs of 27°C. Sunday looks like it will be light showers, with temperatures dropping to 19°C.

What happened last time out?

Norris carried his winning momentum into Brazil and put his McLaren on pole position. The Brit then went on to take a dominant victory in Sunday's race.

He extended the lead in the drivers' championship to 24 points from teammate Piastri with three races of the season remaining.

Verstappen had a remarkable drive after struggling with the car in qualifying. For the race, the Red Bull driver started from the pit lane so the team could fit a new engine and change the car set-up, and ended up recovering to finish third.

Mercedes' Antonelli finished second, with his teammate Russell in fourth.

Who will win this year?

Antonelli clinched his maiden world title last time out, so the pressure will be off his shoulders now after getting the job done in Mexico City. He could also break a few more records including most wins in a maiden championship season.

Verstappen leapfrogged to second in the title standings and won the race last week to take his third victory this season, so could be a threat to Mercedes.

Hamilton sealed his first pole position last time out for Ferrari and looked more comfortable in the car. The seven-time world champion, who is an honorary citizen of Brazil, has always been one to watch at this track.

Despite the drivers' championship being wrapped up, the constructors' is all to play for. Mercedes are in mathematical contention to win it in Brazil and will be looking to maximise points from both Antonelli and Russell.

The team need to outscore Ferrari by three points or more.

stories.headline: Thunder to retire Russell Westbrook's No. 0
stories.summary: The Thunder will retire Russell Westbrook's No. 0 this season. The former MVP played the first 11 of his 18 seasons in Oklahoma City.
stories.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder announced they will retire Russell Westbrook's No. 0 in the rafters on Feb. 7.

Westbrook was a first-round pick of the organization in 2008, just days before the team officially became the Thunder after relocating from Seattle.

Westbrook played the first 11 years of his 18-season career in OKC and paired with Kevin Durant to turn the young Thunder into one of the best teams in the league. However, after Durant's free agent departure following the 2015-16 season, Westbrook's stature in Oklahoma City grew.

The next season, Westbrook became the first player to average a triple-double for an entire season since Oscar Robertson, going for 31.6 points, 10.7 rebounds and 10.4 assists, and was named league MVP. He continued to average a triple-double for the following two seasons, his final ones with the Thunder.

"Many players make an impact but only great players leave a legacy. Russell Westbrook's legacy was built both on the court and in the community," Thunder executive vice president and general manager Sam Presti said in a statement Monday. "His mindset was relentless, his commitment deep. For all those reasons, Oklahomans consider him one of their own and his number will be raised to the rafters, in Oklahoma City forever."

OKC traded Westbrook to the Houston Rockets ahead of the 2019-20 season, part of an offseason that saw the team move away from the Westbrook-Paul George pairing and establish the foundation for the franchise's current run of success.

After a season in Houston, Westbrook bounced around the league playing with the Washington Wizards, Los Angeles Lakers, LA Clippers, Denver Nuggets and Sacramento Kings.

A nine-time All-Star and member of the NBA's 75th anniversary team in 2021, Westbrook announced his retirement this offseason. His No. 0 will be the second jersey retired by the Thunder joining Nick Collison's No. 4.

stories.headline: Lightning star Nikita Kucherov says trade request not about money
stories.summary: Lightning star Nikita Kucherov says his trade request is not about the money.
stories.body:
Tampa Bay Lightning star Nikita Kucherov said his trade request is not about seeking a big payday.

"It was never about the money to me," he told reporters Monday. "It was more about poor communication and respect. Over the last four months we have only had two conversations. [General manager] Julien [BriseBois] in them made clear I'm free to walk on July 1."

That's when Kucherov can become an unrestricted free agent. He is making $9.5 million in the last year of his eight-year deal but could be looking at twice that much going forward after winning two Hart Trophies and two Stanley Cups in 13 seasons with the Lightning.

After word of Kucherov's trade request became public Friday, BriseBois put out a statement saying, "We unequivocally have no intention of trading Nikita."

Coach Jon Cooper said Saturday: "Kuch is 100% a part of this team. He wants to be a part of this team for this season, and he is committed to be with the group that loves him and the group he loves."

A clearly subdued Kucherov echoed that sentiment Monday.

"For now, I'm part of the team, and I will do everything I can to help my teammates win," he said.

He added that Tampa, Florida, has become his home and that he has raised his kids there. He said he's "forever grateful to this organization."

But he did not back off his trade request.

ESPN's Greg Wyshynski contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Messi tracker: Goals, assists, key moments in 2026
stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 46
Goals: 41
Assists: 19

Nov. 1: New England Revolution 1-2 Inter Miami

Messi once again provided the magic touch for Miami, this time to ensure his team's spot in the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Herons' marquee star set up a goal and scored the winner as Miami leapfrogged New England into second place in the Eastern Conference with one game remaining in the MLS regular season.

After going behind to a Dániel Gazdag goal, Miami responded with a strike from Germán Berterame -- set up by a deft backward header from Messi -- before the 39-year-old scored the winner in the 83rd minute. Sumptuous stuff.

Oct. 28: FC Cincinnati 2-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists for Messi in what was an eventful 2-2 draw with FC Cincinnati on Wednesday night.

Luis Suárez scored in the 61st minute to give Miami a 1-0 lead, and then the reigning MLS Cup champions needed some late-game heroics to salvage a point. They still fell to third in the Eastern Conference, after New England beat Red Bull New York 3-2 on Wednesday.

Oct. 24: Red Bull New York 2-0 Inter Miami
It has been an eventful few days for Messi. Just a day before the match, he traveled to Spain to receive the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports, becoming the first individual soccer player to earn the honor.

He then returned to the United States and joined his teammates in New Jersey, starting on the bench before coming on in the 56th minute. However, he was unable to make an impact as the hosts secured a 2-0 victory, ending Miami's three-game winning streak.

Oct. 17: Atlanta United 1-3 Inter Miami
Messi scored twice in four minutes as Miami won 3-1 in Atlanta.

After Germán Berterame opened the scoring just before halftime, Messi doubled Miami's lead in the 56th minute, exchanging passes with Berterame before weaving past a defender and firing a low left-footed shot into the net.

Messi struck again in the 60th minute, latching on to a pass from Luis Suárez before beating his marker and slotting past goalkeeper Lucas Hoyos. The brace took Messi's MLS-leading tally to 25 goals for the season, while Miami extended its winning streak to three matches.

Oct. 14: Inter Miami 2-0 NYCFC
No goals, but after a scoreless first half, Messi helped break the deadlock by setting up Rodrigo De Paul for the opening goal. Germán Berterame later doubled Miami's advantage as the Herons secured their second consecutive win and clinched a spot in the MLS playoffs.

Oct. 10: Inter Miami 4-0 D.C. United

Back in the pink of Inter Miami, and back in the goals for Messi.

His two strikes sealed an emphatic 4-0 win for the Herons over D.C. United at Nu Stadium on Saturday night.

After Luis Suárez had Miami 2-0 up after 39 minutes Messi scored his first in the 47th, retrieving a pass from the Uruguayan before tapping in a shot inside the right post.

Messi then padded the hosts' lead in the 60th minute, latching on to Rodrigo De Paul's pass, before dribbling inside the area, eluding two United defenders and firing past goalkeeper Sean Johnson with a shot from 12 yards.

Oct. 6: Argentina 3-0 Benin

It was an emotionally charged night in Buenos Aires as Messi played his final international match for Argentina, the team that he had led to World Cup glory and two Copa América titles as captain.

The friendly match at the Estadio Monumental was goalless at halftime, but just a few minutes after the break Messi's in-swinging corner from the left was rattled home on the volley by Nicolás Otamendi.

Then, on the hour mark, Messi spotted Nico Paz in space 25 yards from goal. He fed a square pass with the outside of his boot to the Como player, who curled in a classy finish.

But the night undoubtedly belonged to Messi, and he fired a penalty into the top corner to cap off his 208th and final senior appearance for his country with his 126th goal.

Sep. 27: Columbus Crew 2-1 Inter Miami
Before heading to Argentina for his final international match, Messi gave Miami fans something to savor in Ohio.

From a set piece wide on the right wing and with most of those in the stadium, including those in the Columbus defense, surely expecting a cross, Messi's left foot sent the ball curling wickedly into the far top corner of the net.

Messi had chances to add to that tally in the second half but was denied from distance by Columbus goalkeeper Patrick Schulte and put another effort into the side netting.

Then Jamal Thiaré scored in the eighth minute of second-half stoppage time to give the Columbus Crew a stunning 2-1 win.

Sep. 20: Inter Miami 2-2 San Diego FC

Messi's sublime curling free kick was not enough to inspire the Herons to a win against San Diego on Sunday night.

After falling behind to an Anders Dreyer goal in the 12th minute, 39-year-old Messi levelled the scores with beautiful set-piece shot in the 24th minute. His well-hit effort evaded a number of attackers and defenders before sneaking in at the far post.

Miami thought they'd won the match after Luiz Suarez fired the hosts ahead in the 74th minute, only for Dreyer to nab his second goal of the game and ensure the points were shared.

Sep. 16: Inter Miami 2-0 Cruz Azul

Another day, another trophy for Messi.

The Argentine master scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami as the Herons defeated Cruz Azul 2-0 on Wednesday night to win the Campeones Cup.

Messi opened the scoring in the 24th minute, heading in a cross from Luis Suárez, before turning provider for Casemiro -- sending in a corner for the Brazilian to nod home.

Sep. 12: Inter Miami 2-2 Nashville SC
In a matchup between the two best teams in the Eastern Conference, the action went end to end, with Messi getting on the scoresheet for Miami's second goal off a Rodrigo De Paul assist as he continues to lead the Golden Boot race.

Ultimately, the teams settled for a point apiece, as the hosts failed to close the gap on Nashville at the top of the table.

Sep. 9: Chicago Fire 1-1 Inter Miami

Two or Europe's greatest club players took center stage in one of the United States' most iconic American football stadiums on Wednesday -- and a record crowd came out to watch.

Ex-Bayern Munich and Barcelona star Robert Lewandowski scored a trademark acrobatic goal in the 10th minute to give the Fire an early lead at the NFL home of the Chicago Bears.

But Inter Miami drew level shortly after halftime when Casemiro, another of the game's stars with a long history of playing in Europe before moving to MLS, headed home a Messi cross from a corner kick to make it 1-1.

The assist was Messi's league-leading 13th of the season. He also has league 18 goals and is the first player in MLS history with 30-plus goal contributions in three separate seasons.

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.

stories.headline: AFL 2027 fixture: Five must-watch games in the first month
stories.summary: The 2027 AFL fixture has been released. So, to whet your appetite for the upcoming season, we've picked out the five must-watch games from the opening month.
stories.body:
The 2027 AFL fixture has been released. So, to whet your appetite for the upcoming season, we've picked out the five must-watch games from the opening month of action.

Get the popcorn ready and get set to enjoy these absolute belters in the new year.

5. Port Adelaide vs. Western Bulldogs - Round 4, Adelaide Oval, Sunday, April 8, 7:40pm (AEDT)
Make no mistake, when Zak Butters returns to Adelaide Oval to face his old mob for the first time since departing, it's going to be incredibly spicy.

In a move that shocked absolutely nobody, Butters left Port Adelaide during the 2026 trade period, inking a long-term deal with the Western Bulldogs. It's a brutal blow for the Power, and his ex-teammates will be sure to give him a hard time when they share the field in Round 4. You just know it's going to be on for young and old!

The AFL also made the move to schedule this blockbuster game as the closer to next year's Gather Round. It means far more bodies will be in Adelaide that weekend and a greater number of eyeballs on the clash.

4. Hawthorn vs. Geelong - Round 2, MCG, Monday, March 29, 3:15pm (AEDT)
The traditional Easter Monday clash between the Hawks and Cats is always on our shortlist of early season must-watch games, and next year will be no exception.

Both of these clubs are in the premiership window. Both clubs have added high-profile players this offseason. Both clubs have fanbases that bring an electric energy to Easter Monday at the MCG.

This one is also set to be a fascinating coaching battle between Chris Scott and Sam Mitchell, two of the game's best tacticians, who will go head-to-head just as much as the players on the field.

3. Fremantle vs. Western Bulldogs - Round 1, Optus Stadium, Thursday, March 18, 8:10pm (AEDT)
This Round 1 game in the west is simply oozing with intrigue.

Of course, the question on everyone's mind is how the Dockers back up after having this year's premiership ripped away from them in harrowing circumstances. Does it galvanise the club? Will we see 'Wharfie Time'? Surely not!

For the Bulldogs, they landed the biggest fish of the off-season in superstar midfielder Zak Butters. This will be the first opportunity to watch him play in his new colours, lining up in the middle alongside skipper Marcus Bontempelli and Ed Richards.

2. Brisbane vs. Collingwood - Round 2, Gabba, Thursday, March 25, 7:50pm (AEDT)
Reigning premier Brisbane will unfurl its latest flag in Round 2 when it hosts Collingwood in its first home game of the season, a clash that has blockbuster written all over it.

The Lions are looking to become just the second team ever to win four consecutive flags (joining, you guessed it, Collingwood from 1927 to 1930) but will be doing it without superstar midfielder Lachie Neale. The two-time Brownlow medallist departed for the Magpies this offseason, making this early season contest between the two clubs extra intriguing.

Plus, any opportunity to watch current Brownlow medallist Nick Daicos play footy is reason in itself to tune in!

1. Hawthorn vs. Brisbane - Round 1, MCG, Friday, March 19, 7:40pm (AEDT)
Thankfully we don't have to wait long for the Hawks and Lions -- quite possibly the competition's two best teams -- to square off in 2027. And if this game delivers even 70% of what these sides dished up in this year's epic preliminary final, then we're in for an absolute treat!

Many have labelled Brisbane's thrilling win over Hawthorn this past September as the greatest game of footy played this century. That in itself should be enough of a reason for their next clash to simply be must-watch.

There will be extra intrigue with both teams given this clash falls in Round 1. For the Lions, they will be looking to navigate life without both superstar midfielder Lachie Neale and master coach Chris Fagan, while the Hawks will be attempting to integrate recruits Zach Merrett and Ben King into their line-up.

stories.headline: Unlikely winner emerges from luckless Samoan blow
stories.summary: Ronald Volkman is set to go from Dragons discard to starting in a World Cup semi-final against Australia in the space of 12 months.
stories.body:
Chanel Harris-Tavita's luckless World Cup run looks set to play into the hands of Ronald Volkman, who looms as the obvious candidate to fill Samoa's playmaking void for their semi-final meeting with Australia.

Harris-Tavita was knocked out cold in the last World Cup final four years ago and is now long-odds to play again for Samoa this campaign.

The Warriors' No.6 strained his hamstring while taking a shot at goal in Sunday's 20-18 group stage loss to Tonga.

Parramatta half Volkman made an instant impact, scoring a try after replacing Harris-Tavita from the bench, and he will step in against the Kangaroos.

Volkman's rise to a likely Samoan starting jersey caps a terrific season for the 24-year-old after he was dumped by St George Illawarra in 2024 with concerns over a long-term shoulder issue.

Samoa face Australia on Sunday at Sydney's Allianz Stadium after their narrow loss to the Tongans dumped England out of the tournament on points differential.

"Ronald's done a great job, he did a fantastic job last week for us in the win over Papua New Guinea," Samoa coach Ben Gardiner said.

"He came on at the back end of the game, in a slightly different role for a different reason and he did a really good job when he came on.

"I thought he brought great energy, I thought his speed in the line really put pressure on the Tongan team.

"We've got trust in every player in our team, so it doesn't matter who goes on.

"The guys that are in our squad, we've got complete trust in them."

The 24-year-old Volkman is likely to be the target of heavy traffic from the Kangaroos' edge forwards as the two sides renew a rivalry that has simmered since the World Cup final four years ago.

Samoa have yet to beat Australia in a Test across fives meetings and lost 38-12 in their last international three years ago.

"Their form's been very strong, very strong and they've got fantastic players," Gardiner said.

"They've got players that have played a lot of games for the Kangaroos and are in a really good position at the moment.

"They've won three footy matches on the trot, and they're going to be a really hard side to beat next week.

"If we hold on to the ball and we complete better than 66 per cent that'll give us a good opportunity to pick up on some of those things we need to work on."
